chunk_findings.detail: `landed_leftovers_only` skips the file-content check for every merge commit: when `len(parents) > 1`, it only verifies that each parent after the first is an ancestor of `base`, then `continue`s. A merge commit’s own merge resolution can add arbitrary non-pin files while satisfying that check. Example: `base`/main is at B and `item.merged_sha` is B; create merge commit M with `git merge --no-ff --no-commit B`, edit `src/foo.py`, and commit. Both parents of M are ancestors of `base`, so `base..HEAD` contains only M. The function sees M, finds the second parent is on `base`, `continue`s, returns `True`, and `_classify` marks the tree `action = "remove"`. Cleanup then deletes the worktree, losing `src/foo.py`, which exists nowhere on `base`. The merge commit itself must be diffed (`diff-tree -m` or equivalent) and required to contain only pinned files, otherwise a merge commit is unsafe to classify as “merge-main/pin commits only”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cleanup.py:landed_leftovers_only

chunk_findings.detail: When the re-proof fails because the worktree is “no longer only landed leftovers”, `_remove_planned` returns a `kept ...` report line but does not update `t.action`/`t.kind`/`t.done`. `apply` receives `plan` by reference, and the same function updates `t` in the `dispose_tree(...).outcome == "refused"` path explicitly so later consumers of `plan` see the final decision (the function docstring also says `t` is updated when kept). chunk_findings.detail: `landed_leftovers_only` treats a root commit as safe to delete even when it contains arbitrary non-pin files. chunk_findings.detail: `files.out.split()` splits `git diff-tree --name-only` output on arbitrary whitespace, but the command does not use `-z`, so Git paths containing spaces are not parsed as single path names. This can misclassify commits. Concretely, with `pins == ["a.pin", "b.pin"]`, one non-pin file literally named `a.pin b.pin` is emitted as a single line `a.pin b.pin`; `.split()` yields `{"a.pin", "b.pin"}`, which is a subset of `pins`, so `landed_leftovers_only` returns True and cleanup offers removal for a commit that touched no actual pin file. Use `-z` and split on NUL to make the comparison path-accurate.

chunk_findings.detail: The commit loop now iterates over `loose`, which contains both named blobs and orphan blobs (`loose, orphans = split_loose_blobs(repo)`), and does `taken[rel] = (repo / rel).read_bytes()`. chunk_findings.detail: The TOCTOU already reported is still present in the new `landed_tip` guard. `a = 0 if landed_tip and a > 0 and head_sha(wt.path) == landed_tip else a` reads HEAD at that instant. If another process commits `C2` in the same worktree after this check, the branch is no longer "only landed leftovers," but the function proceeds to an unforced `git worktree remove`. Git does not refuse a clean worktree merely because its branch advanced, so it deletes the worktree even though it now points at `C2`. The later compare-and-delete is not a remedy: the branch ref survives, but the worktree is already gone. The doc sentence "a later one is work, and refuses" is false under this interleaving.

chunk_findings.detail: `ddflow job end` with no job argument and no `--all-finished` reaches `_job_end` and calls `AJ.job_end(c.repo, a.job or "", ..., all_finished=a.all_finished, ...)`. Since `a.job` is `None` and `a.all_finished` is `False`, this passes `""` as the job. The API's bulk branch is entered whenever `job` is empty, as established by the earlier confirmed finding on `ddflow/api/jobs.py`, so this command bulk-collects every finished job across all items instead of rejecting the missing job id. The CLI should require at least one of `a.job` or `a.all_finished` before calling the API; otherwise an accidental no-argument `job end` becomes a destructive bulk operation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/knowledge.py:_job_end

chunk_findings.detail: The previous ordering concern is only partly answered. The probe now inserts J2 before J1, so a naive `list(st.jobs)` implementation would fail, but it still gives both jobs plain string `started_at` values: `"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"` and `""`. The real missing-start-time value is likely `None`, and a `collect_finished` that sorts with `key=lambda j: j.started_at` still passes this test because Python compares two strings without the dangerous mixed `None`/datetime comparison. A job with `started_at=None` plus a datetime-started job is the actual input that would expose the bug; this test would not catch it.

chunk_findings.detail: The requested flag in the intent is `ddflow job end --all-exited [--item X]`, but the new test file documents and exercises only `--all-finished`. Every CLI invocation here uses `--all-finished`, and there is no test that `--all-exited` is accepted. A CLI that never accepts the requested `--all-exited` flag passes this test suite, so the original user-facing requirement is untested and can remain missing.
